rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Big Idea match (judge-owned criterion, not a numbered compendium rule — file has no ## Big Idea of its own; checked against module file earn-the-trust.md's Big Idea)
rules_evaluated.evidence: Module Big Idea: "one skill you author through conversation with Claude does the quality work... ships personal first, with a clear path to team promotion through a human conversation later." Exercise's own framing ("The point") and Phase 3/"Decide if it graduates to the team" sections instantiate this almost bullet-for-bullet: conversation-authored, self-critiqued, invoked, shipped personal-first, team PR gated on a human conversation.

"The point: Test strategy authored generically is a pyramid diagram. Test strategy authored on your codebase, through conversation, with one forced self-critique and one invocation on a real feature, is a skill a teammate can adopt" — matches module Meta mood target verbatim in spirit ("earned trust, culminating... I shipped it somewhere my teammates read"). M3's mood is 'culminating' per the module's own Meta block, so full resolution within this file (not stewing into M4) is the correct shape, not a violation.

"The grade is biased by design. Claude invoked the skill it just helped author, then graded the result in the same context window: same-window self-charity... convenient over rigorous" and "If the strategy reads generic, sharpen the skill, not the output. A weak output is usually a weak skill" frame the self-critique as not-yet-known/diagnostic, never as the student having done something wrong. No shame language anywhere in the self-critique beats.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode
rules_evaluated.evidence: Framing verbs lead throughout ("Author," "push back," "disclose," "invoke," "sharpen," "ship"); failure words ("theatre," "generic," "weak") appear only as diagnostic pivots inside body prose (e.g. "Authoring without invocation is theatre"), never as the title or lead framing of a Big-Idea-shaped claim. Note: file carries no ## Big Idea / Key Concepts / What You'll Learn heading of its own (those live in the module file), so this rule is assessed against general body framing rather than a structured section — still clean.

"What this sets up" section's M4/M6 forward references match the strategy doc precisely: M4's audit subagent reads "the M3 test-strategy skill" (strategy doc M4 Phase 2) ↔ file's "Module 4 reads this skill as part of the system you have"; M6's second skill can take "verifier / judge / gap-finder" shape (strategy doc M6 row) ↔ file's "M6 authors a verifier skill the same way you authored this one." "Decide if it graduates to the team" matches "Team PR is a strong follow-up... starts with a human conversation... agents don't unilaterally change shared team infrastructure" near-verbatim. Exercise correctly keeps Ex3 in the main thread with no subagent framing, matching the strategy doc's explicit design ("Ex3 (test-strategy authoring) stays in the main thread — one-question-at-a-time conversation is not a subagent job, and the contrast is half the pedagogy"). No downstream teaching moment (Ronacher's three-pattern, M5/M6 content) is taught early — only named as a forward pointer.

File instances multiple AE101 recurring themes in its own language even though it carries no standalone ## Key Concepts heading (that section is assembled at module level from all three M3 exercises): self-aware + grain-of-salt ("The grade is biased by design... same-window self-charity"); compounding ("The move repeats and gets faster"); capture-your-world ("push back when Claude offers a default you don't like... the push-back is where the skill gets its codebase truth"). ≥3 theme-instances present in module's own voice.
